issues.t: Engine burns oil from faulty piston rings
issues.sym: You need to add oil between changes (some owners report about 2 quarts every 1,200 miles), a low oil message, knocking or brief power loss, and fouled or broken spark plugs.
issues.why: The oil control rings on these engines do not drain oil off the cylinder walls well, so oil burns in the combustion chamber and can damage pistons and plugs. Volvo's bulletin TJ31216 replaces the pistons and rings, and a class action covers 2013-2016 Volvos with these engines.
issues.next: Check the oil level every fill-up and never let it run low. Ask a Volvo dealer for an oil consumption test and the piston/ring bulletin, and keep records in case of warranty or settlement coverage.

issues.t: 12V battery drains and car won't start
issues.sym: A battery warning or 12V battery message, slow cranking, or a dead battery after the car sits.
issues.why: These cars have many modules that stay awake after shutdown, and Volvo has issued several bulletins on 12V battery messages, testing and drain (including one caused by a service Wi-Fi connection).
issues.next: Have the battery tested with Volvo's method and the software checked before buying parts. If the car sits a lot, use a battery maintainer.

issues.t: Vibration or shudder when braking
issues.sym: The steering wheel or pedal shakes when you brake, especially from highway speed.
issues.why: Volvo has a bulletin for braking shudder; the fix is new front brake pads. Some owners also found rotors out of spec.
issues.next: Have the front brakes measured and inspected. Ask the dealer about bulletin 36202 if the car is under warranty.

issues.t: Infotainment screen reboots or false alerts
issues.sym: The center screen goes blank or restarts while driving, the sound system makes static or screeching noises, or warnings appear for no reason.
issues.why: Software faults in the Sensus infotainment unit. Volvo issued bulletins with software reloads for reboots and audio noise.
issues.next: Ask the dealer for the latest software. A frozen screen can often be restarted by holding the home button.

issues.t: Center screen stuck restarting (Google system)
issues.sym: The center display hangs in recovery mode, shows "Searching for GPS", or will not load.
issues.why: Software faults in the newer Google-based infotainment system. Volvo's bulletins say reloading the infotainment software often fixes it.
issues.next: Try restarting the system with the home button. If it keeps happening, a dealer can reload the software.

issues.t: Steering assist or key-not-found messages
issues.sym: A "Steering Assistance Temporarily Reduced" message at start-up, or a key-not-found message with the key inside.
issues.why: Volvo bulletins cover these false messages; the steering message at cranking does not actually reduce assistance.
issues.next: If steering feels normal, mention it at your next service so the dealer can apply the bulletin fix. If steering really feels heavy, stop and get it checked.

issues.t: Panoramic roof rattles when opening
issues.sym: A rattle or creak from the glass roof when opening it or over bumps.
issues.why: Volvo issued repeated bulletins for panoramic roof rattle on these cars.
issues.next: Ask the dealer about the roof rattle bulletin.

issues.t: Check engine light for misfire fixed by software
issues.sym: A check engine light with a misfire code (P030098).
issues.why: Volvo found a software cause for this code and says not to replace parts; a software update fixes it.
issues.next: If the engine runs smoothly, book a dealer visit for the update. If the light flashes or the engine shakes, reduce speed and get it checked soon.

issues.t: Knocking from the rear electric motor (T8)
issues.sym: A knocking noise from the rear on the plug-in hybrid.
issues.why: A bulletin for the long-range plug-in hybrid adds a repair kit to the rear electric drive unit to stop the knock.
issues.next: Have a dealer confirm the source and install the repair kit.

issues.t: Sunroof drains clog and leak water inside
issues.sym: Wet front footwells or damp headliner after rain or a car wash.
issues.why: The drain channels and screens around the sunroof clog with debris, so water overflows into the cabin.
issues.next: Clear the sunroof drain channels and screens. Dry the carpet quickly, because water near the floor can damage wiring and modules.

issues.t: AWD angle gear grinding noise
issues.sym: A grinding noise from the front of the car, especially when turning at highway speed.
issues.why: The angle gear (power take-off) that sends power to the rear wheels on AWD cars can wear. One Cross Country owner needed three visits before the dealer replaced it.
issues.next: Grinding that changes with turning should be checked soon. Ask the shop to inspect the angle gear and its fluid, not just the wheel bearings.

issues.t: Audio module stops working
issues.sym: No sound or a dead radio and media system.
issues.why: The audio module can fail; one owner reports replacing it at about 61,000 miles.
issues.next: Check fuses and try a system reset first; if it stays dead, a shop can test the module.

issues.t: Door can look closed but not latch (recall)
issues.sym: A door that will not latch, needs repeated closing, or a door-ajar warning.
issues.why: Recall 19V-849: a part inside the door latch can break, so a door may seem shut but not be latched.
issues.next: Check every door is fully latched before driving. Get the free latch replacement.

issues.t: Front seat belt anchor cable can break (recall)
issues.sym: Frayed or damaged cable at the side of the front seat, or no symptom.
issues.why: Recall 20V-378: the steel cable that anchors the front belt can fatigue and may not hold in a crash.
issues.next: Run your VIN; the repair is free and important.

issues.t: Passenger seat belt buckle can come loose (recall)
issues.sym: A loose front passenger buckle.
issues.why: Recall 16V-798: the stud holding the front passenger buckle can loosen.
issues.next: Get the free recall repair.

issues.t: Starter fuse can blow with stop/start (recall)
issues.sym: The engine does not restart after an automatic stop at a light.
issues.why: Recall 15V-555: the starter fuse can blow during stop/start use.
issues.next: Turn off stop/start until the free recall is done.

issues.t: Side airbags may not inflate in a crash (recall)
issues.sym: Usually no symptom.
issues.why: Recalls 16V-918 and 17V-127: front side airbag initiators may fail to fire.
issues.next: Run your VIN and get the free fix.

issues.t: Emergency call may not send GPS location (recall)
issues.sym: No symptom until an emergency call is made.
issues.why: Recall 18V-800: a software error can stop the car's location from reaching emergency services.
issues.next: Get the free software update.

issues.t: Automatic emergency braking may not detect obstacles (recall)
issues.sym: No obvious symptom; the system may not brake for an obstacle.
issues.why: Recall 20V-144: a mismatch between software and hardware can stop obstacle detection.
issues.next: Do not rely on auto braking until the free software update is done.

issues.t: Fuel pump fuse can blow and stall the engine (recall)
issues.sym: The engine stalls or will not start.
issues.why: Recall 21V-414: the low-pressure fuel pump can blow its fuse and fail.
issues.next: If the car stalls, get to safety and use hazards. Check your VIN for the free repair.

issues.t: Loose screw can lock the steering (recall)
issues.sym: Steering that binds or catches.
issues.why: Recall 23V-001 (V60 Cross Country): a screw can fall into the steering gear housing and lock the wheel.
issues.next: If steering binds, stop driving and have it towed. Get the free inspection.

issues.t: Airbag control unit may come loose in a crash (recall)
issues.sym: No symptom.
issues.why: Recall 21V-001: the airbag control unit may detach from the body in a crash.
issues.next: Run your VIN and book the free repair.

issues.t: Seat belt may not hold a child seat (recall)
issues.sym: A belt that does not stay locked when installing a child seat.
issues.why: Recall 21V-682: belt retractors can leave child-seat locking mode too early.
issues.next: Use LATCH anchors for child seats if possible and get the free repair.

issues.t: Plug-in hybrid battery can short circuit (recall)
issues.sym: Usually no warning.
issues.why: Recall 25V-179: a high-voltage battery module can short when fully charged and parked, which is a fire risk.
issues.next: Follow Volvo's recall instructions about charging and parking, and get the free repair.

issues.t: Gas engine may not start on plug-in hybrid (recall)
issues.sym: Loss of drive power because the engine does not start.
issues.why: Recall 22V-793: engine computer software can stop the engine from starting.
issues.next: Get the free software update.

issues.t: ABS and stability control may switch off (recall)
issues.sym: ABS, stability or traction control warnings.
issues.why: Recall 23V-012: a brake module diagnostic error can turn off ABS and stability control.
issues.next: Drive gently and leave extra distance. Get the free update.

issues.t: Backup camera image may not appear (recall)
issues.sym: A blank screen in reverse.
issues.why: Recalls 25V-282 and 25V-908: a software fault can stop the rear camera image showing.
issues.next: Use mirrors and look back. Get the free software update.

issues.t: Braking can drop out in one-pedal or B mode (recall)
issues.sym: Less or no braking when coasting downhill in B mode or one-pedal mode.
issues.why: Recall 25V-392: a brake module software fault can cut braking in these modes.
issues.next: Avoid B and one-pedal modes until the free software update is done; use the brake pedal.
